title: Top-k Filtering and Token Probabilities
body:
When a language model picks a word, it starts by scoring all possible choices. These raw scores are turned into percentages that add up to one hundred.

A method called top-k filtering keeps only a few top choices and throws away the rest.

Look at the chart to see how filtering changes the numbers for each remaining word.

```rh-diagram

The other tokens drop to zero, and each kept token gets a bigger share.","kind":"bar-chart","unit":"%","variant":"grouped","categories":["on","near","under","by","in"],"series":[{"label":"Full softmax","values":[42,28,16,8,6]},{"label":"Top-2 renormalized","values":[60,40,0,0,0]}]}}
```

Because the rejected words are removed, their percentages are set to zero. The remaining words share out the leftover space so their percentages add up to one hundred again.

This means the reported chance of picking the top word goes up after filtering.
